questions.worked_solution:
Let's denote the vectors that span the subspace $H$ as ${h}_{1}$ and ${h}_{2}.$ 

A vector $x=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]$ belongs to ${H}^{⊥}$ if $x\cdot {h}_{1}=0$ and $x\cdot {h}_{2}=0.$ So, we need to solve the following system:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x\cdot {h}_{1}=0 \\ x\cdot {h}_{2}=0\end{aligned}\,⟹\,\{\begin{aligned}6{x}_{1}-9{x}_{2}=0 \\ 4{x}_{1}-6{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

with the augmented matrix $M,$ which we reduce to row echelon form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}6 & -9 & 0 \\ 4 & -6 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-\frac{2}{3}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}6 & -9 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, we have $1$ pivot column (the $1$st one), so ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. From the first equation, we get ${x}_{1}=\frac{3}{2}{x}_{2}.$ So, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{2}{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Therefore, our orthogonal complement is

$$
{H}^{⊥}=\{[\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{2}{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]\,:\,{x}_{2}\in R\}.
$$

questions.problem: Given that $u=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b \\ c\end{aligned}]$ is a non-zero  vector that is orthogonal to the set $W=\{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3 \\ 1\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1 \\ -2\end{aligned}]\},$ find the value of $\frac{c}{a+b}.$
questions.worked_solution:
The vector $u$ is orthogonal to the set $W$ if $u\cdot {w}_{1}=0$ and $u\cdot {w}_{2}=0.$ So, we need to solve the following system:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}u\cdot {w}_{1}=0 \\ u\cdot {w}_{2}=0\end{aligned}\,⟹\,\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=0 \\ 3{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}-2{x}_{3}=0\end{aligned}
$$

with the augmented matrix $M,$ which we reduce to row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 1 & 0 \\ 3 & 1 & -2 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 10 & -5 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, we have $2$ pivot columns (the $1$st and $2$nd), so ${x}_{3}$ is a free variable. From the second equation, we get ${x}_{2}=\frac{1}{2}{x}_{3}.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we obtain ${x}_{1}=\frac{1}{2}{x}_{3}.$ So, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}{x}_{3} \\ \frac{1}{2}{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

Setting ${x}_{3}=2,$ we get the vector 
$[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$

Therefore, we obtain $a=1,$ $b=1,$ and $c=2.$

Finally, $\frac{c}{a+b}=\frac{2}{1+1}=1.$

questions.worked_solution:
The vector $u$ is orthogonal to the set $W$ if $u\cdot {w}_{1}=0$ and $u\cdot {w}_{2}=0.$ So, we need to solve the following system:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}u\cdot {w}_{1}=0 \\ u\cdot {w}_{2}=0\end{aligned}\,⟹\,\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2}-{x}_{3}=0 \\ 3{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=0\end{aligned}
$$

with the augmented matrix $M,$ which we reduce to row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & -1 & 0 \\ 3 & 1 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 10 & 4 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, we have $2$ pivot columns (the $1$st and $2$nd), so ${x}_{3}$ is a free variable. From the second equation, we get ${x}_{2}=-\frac{2}{5}{x}_{3}.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we obtain ${x}_{1}=-\frac{1}{5}{x}_{3}.$ So, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{5}{x}_{3} \\ -\frac{2}{5}{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

Setting ${x}_{3}=5$, we get the vector 
$[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -2 \\ 5\end{aligned}].$

Therefore, we obtain $a=-1,$ $b=-2,$ and $c=5.$

Finally, $\frac{b+c}{a}=\frac{-2+5}{-1}=-3.$

questions.problem:
Consider the vector subspace $H=\text{Span}\{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4 \\ -4\end{aligned}]\}.$ Which of the following vectors belong to ${H}^{⊥}?$

$$
{v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -5 \\ -4\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 4 \\ -3\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 4\end{aligned}]
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Let  $h=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4 \\ -4\end{aligned}].$ A vector  $v$ belongs to ${H}^{⊥}$ if $v$ is orthogonal to $h.$ So, we have to find the products ${v}_{i}\cdot h$ for $i=1,2,3.$   

- For ${v}_{1}$, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{1}\cdot h & =4\cdot 1+(-5)\cdot 4+(-4)\cdot (-4)=0 & ✓\end{aligned}
$$

 
So, ${v}_{1}\in {H}^{⊥}.$

- For ${v}_{2}$, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{2}\cdot h & =2\cdot 1+4\cdot 4+(-3)\cdot (-4)=30\ne 0 & \times \end{aligned}
$$

 
So, ${v}_{2}\notin {H}^{⊥}.$

- For ${v}_{3}$, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{3}\cdot h & =1\cdot 1+(-1)\cdot 4+4\cdot (-4)=-19\ne 0 & \times \end{aligned}
$$

So, ${v}_{3}\notin {H}^{⊥}.$

Therefore, the correct answer is "${v}_{1}$  only".
